models.description:
# Model summary

This private model family packages the exact checkpoints used in Jason Matthew Suhari's reproducible one-bit neural-network fault-injection experiment. The experiment searched 35,840 final-layer storage-bit mutations across float32, float16, and symmetric int8 representations of a pinned CIFAR-10 ResNet-20.

# Model characteristics

The upstream model is `cifar10_resnet20` from `chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models`, pinned to source commit `786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a` and checkpoint SHA-256 `4118986f0df73003d572b0e397f0ac7b3f60af1f31aff3d2da164536e36f6ec8`. It has 272,474 parameters and an upstream reported CIFAR-10 top-1 accuracy of 92.60%.

# Data overview

Evaluation uses the canonical 10,000-image CIFAR-10 test split. The source package records all 35,840 searched candidates, the selected mutation, controls, environment details, and per-image predictions.

# Evaluation results

For the float32 variation, flipping exponent bit 30 at `fc.weight[2,8]` changes the stored value from `0x3ea0eb5b` (0.3142956197) to `0x7ea0eb5b` (approximately 1.06949e38). Full-test accuracy changes from 92.60% to 10.03%, and 9,994 of 10,000 predictions become the CIFAR-10 bird class. This is a deliberately narrow empirical result for the pinned checkpoint, layer, data split, and storage representation.

# Provenance

Canonical article: https://blog.jasonsuhari.com/i-flipped-one-bit-in-a-neural-network

Immutable experiment release: https://github.com/jasonsuhari/blog-labs/releases/tag/v1.0.0

Upstream model: https://github.com/chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models

instances.overview: The experiment's float16 storage variation of the pinned CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 checkpoint. Exactly one exponent bit changes in the 640-element float16 final-layer storage control, reproducing the selected bird-collapse result.
instances.usage:
# Model format

`cifar10_resnet20-float16-bird-collapse.pt` is a PyTorch state dictionary for the pinned `cifar10_resnet20` architecture. The final-layer weight tensor is stored as float16; all other tensors retain their upstream dtypes.

# Controlled mutation

The upstream `fc.weight` tensor is converted to the experiment's float16 storage control. Exponent bit 14 at `fc.weight[2,8]` changes from `0x3507` (0.314208984375) to `0x7507` (20592.0). Exactly one of the 640 float16 storage elements differs from that control.

# Recorded evaluation

On the canonical 10,000-image CIFAR-10 test split, the selected variation records 10.05% accuracy and assigns 9,992 predictions (99.92%) to class index 2, `bird`.

# Load the variation

```python
import torch

model = torch.hub.load(
    "chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models:786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a",
    "cifar10_resnet20",
    pretrained=False,
)
state_dict = torch.load(
    "cifar10_resnet20-float16-bird-collapse.pt",
    map_location="cpu",
    weights_only=True,
)
model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
model.eval()
```

PyTorch converts the stored float16 final-layer tensor into the model parameter dtype during loading.

# Provenance

Immutable experiment release: https://github.com/jasonsuhari/blog-labs/releases/tag/v1.0.0

Pinned upstream source: https://github.com/chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models/tree/786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a

instances.overview: A CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 state dictionary with exactly one stored float32 bit changed from the pinned upstream checkpoint. The mutation is the selected winner from a 35,840-candidate final-layer fault-injection search.
instances.usage:
# Model format

`cifar10_resnet20-float32-bird-collapse.pt` is a PyTorch state dictionary for the `cifar10_resnet20` architecture from `chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models` at commit `786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a`.

# Training data

The upstream checkpoint was trained on CIFAR-10. This variation is not retrained; it applies one verified storage-bit mutation to the upstream state dictionary.

# Model inputs

Normalized CIFAR-10 RGB images with the preprocessing used by the pinned upstream model.

# Model outputs

Ten CIFAR-10 class logits. In the recorded 10,000-image test evaluation, 9,994 predictions become class index 2 (`bird`).

# Model usage

```python
import torch

model = torch.hub.load(
    "chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models:786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a",
    "cifar10_resnet20",
    pretrained=False,
)
state_dict = torch.load(
    "cifar10_resnet20-float32-bird-collapse.pt",
    map_location="cpu",
    weights_only=True,
)
model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
model.eval()
```

# Fine-tuning

The artifact is intended for fault-injection and robustness research, not as a drop-in high-accuracy classifier. Fine-tuning would erase the controlled one-bit condition.

# Changelog

Version 1 reproduces the selected float32 mutation at `fc.weight[2,8]`, exponent bit 30: `0x3ea0eb5b` to `0x7ea0eb5b`.

instances.overview: The pinned upstream PyTorch CIFAR model repository used as the unmodified control for the one-bit fault-injection experiment. This linked variation captures the exact source commit that defines the ResNet-20 architecture and downloads the baseline checkpoint.
instances.usage:
# Source and checkpoint

This variation is linked from `chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models` at commit `786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a`. Its `hubconf.py` and package modules define the CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 architecture used by the experiment. The corresponding checkpoint has SHA-256 `4118986f0df73003d572b0e397f0ac7b3f60af1f31aff3d2da164536e36f6ec8` and an upstream reported CIFAR-10 top-1 accuracy of 92.60%.

# Load the unmodified control

```python
import torch

model = torch.hub.load(
    "chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models:786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a",
    "cifar10_resnet20",
    pretrained=True,
)
model.eval()
```

# Inputs and outputs

Inputs are normalized CIFAR-10 RGB images using the preprocessing documented by the upstream project. Outputs are ten CIFAR-10 class logits.

# Relationship to the mutated variation

The `float32-bird-collapse` variation starts from this pinned control checkpoint and changes exactly one stored element at `fc.weight[2,8]` by flipping exponent bit 30. Keeping the upstream source as a separate variation makes the architecture, loading path, and control condition independently auditable.

# Provenance

Pinned source: https://github.com/chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models/tree/786c16252c0fc58ee9adac063f8337cc4a7a497a

Checkpoint: https://github.com/chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models/releases/download/resnet/cifar10_resnet20-4118986f.pt

Experiment release: https://github.com/jasonsuhari/blog-labs/releases/tag/v1.0.0

# AgentWorld 35B-A3B

A 35 billion parameter model with 3 billion active parameters (A3B) in GGUF quantized format.

## Variants

- **Q4_K_M**: Standard quantization without MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) head
- **Q4_K_XL-MTP**: Extended quantization with MTP head for improved inference

## Format

GGUF (GPT-Generated Unified Format) for use with llama.cpp and compatible runtimes.

instances.usage:
# Usage

Load with llama.cpp or compatible GGUF runtime:

```bash
./llama-cli -m Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf
```

What is Qwopus3.6-27B-v2?
🪐 Qwopus3.6-27B-v2 is a reasoning-enhanced dense language model built on top of Qwen3.6-27B. By leveraging a multi-stage curriculum learning pipeline and augmented with Trace Inversion datasets (claude-opus-4.6/4.7-traceInversion), it reverse-engineers the compressed "Reasoning Bubbles" of commercial LLMs into structured, step-by-step synthetic reasoning traces, successfully eliminating logical shortcuts and knowledge fractures.

Vision & Tool Calling Support: Qwopus3.6-27B-v2 natively supports vision and tool-use capabilities. To enable vision functionality, download mmproj.gguf from the GGUF Repository and place it in the same directory as the main .gguf file.

Community Release Notice: Qwopus3.6-27B-v2 is an experimental community release and has not undergone complete safety evaluations or standard benchmarking. It is intended solely for research and exploration.

Context Length and Long-Context Usage
During fine-tuning, this model was trained with a maximum sequence length of 32K tokens. The training data mixture was also constructed around samples up to 32K tokens, so the "Context Length Distribution" shown in this model card reflects the fine-tuning data distribution rather than a hard architectural limit.

The model still inherits the native long-context capability of the Qwen3.6 base model. Therefore, longer context windows such as 128K or 256K may be available in compatible inference runtimes, depending on the backend and configuration.

For practical long-context inference beyond 32K, especially when using llama.cpp / GGUF, it is recommended to enable RoPE/YaRN scaling instead of only increasing n_ctx / --ctx-size. Directly setting a larger context window without RoPE scaling may work in some cases, but it can be less stable and may not achieve the expected long-context performance.

This is consistent with Qwen community guidance for long-context GGUF usage: 128K context generally requires YaRN/RoPE scaling, and it is not necessarily enabled by default in llama.cpp. For example, Qwen maintainers have noted that "128K context length needs YaRN" and that it should be explicitly enabled when supported by the runtime.
Reference: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-GGUF/discussions/2

Community feedback also suggests that RoPE/YaRN scaling can improve long-context stability for this model family. One user reported that, on HermesAgent-20, Qwopus3.6-35B-A3B-v1 performed better when extending from 32K to 128K via RoPE scaling than when directly setting a 128K context window without scaling, with scores of 83 vs. 72 in their setup. This result may vary depending on the backend, quantization type, KV cache settings, hardware, and benchmark configuration, but it is consistent with the recommendation to use RoPE/YaRN scaling for contexts beyond 32K.

Example llama.cpp configuration for extending from 32K to 128K:

./llama-server \
  -m model.gguf \
  --ctx-size 131072 \
  --rope-scaling yarn \
  --rope-scale 4 \
  --yarn-orig-ctx 32768
For 256K context, users may need to adjust the scaling factor accordingly and validate the result in their own workload:

./llama-server \
  -m model.gguf \
  --ctx-size 262144 \
  --rope-scaling yarn \
  --rope-scale 8 \
  --yarn-orig-ctx 32768
Please note that long-context behavior may vary depending on the inference backend, quantization type, KV cache settings, available memory, and task type. For best results, users should benchmark their own target workload when using contexts beyond 32K.

models.description:
CorpIntel-HR-Agent is an instruction-tuned 3B parameter language model fine-tuned on meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). The model evaluates heterogeneous employee telemetry—such as commute friction, salary trajectory, overtime burden, and job satisfaction—to model attrition risk and synthesize structured Managerial Intervention Plans.

Unlike basic binary classification tools that only output a risk percentage, CorpIntel-HR-Agent generates explicit step-by-step reasoning traces detailing why an employee is a flight risk and what concrete steps leadership can take to retain them.

Developer: Asad Ullah Dogar

Model Type: PEFT / LoRA Adapter (Causal LM)

Base Model: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct

Language(s): English (en)

License: Apache 2.0

Platform: Adaption Labs AutoScientist Engine

Dataset: CorpIntel-Attrition-Reasoning-v1 (33,000+ augmented rows)

Compute: 4x NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs

instances.usage:
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from peft import PeftModel

base_model_id = "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct"
adapter_id = "asadullahdogar/corpintel-hr-agent"

# Load tokenizer and base model
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(base_model_id)
base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    base_model_id,
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map="auto"
)

# Load fine-tuned LoRA adapter
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, adapter_id)

# Sample HR telemetry input
prompt = """<|start_header_id|>system<|end_header_id|>
You are an elite HR Business Partner AI. Your objective is to evaluate heterogeneous employee telemetry to model attrition risk and generate a Managerial Intervention Plan.<|eot_id|>
<|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>
Evaluate Candidate: Sales Executive | Travel: Frequently | Distance From Home: 24 miles | Monthly Income: 3200 | OverTime: Yes | JobSatisfaction: 1 | YearsSinceLastPromotion: 4<|eot_id|>
<|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>"""

inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512, temperature=0.3)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))

models.description:
# Model Summary

This LightGBM model predicts whether an existing health insurance customer will purchase a vehicle insurance cross-sell (Response=1). Trained on 381k customer records with demographic, vehicle, and policy features, it outputs a probability score for ranking customers by upsell propensity. Intended for marketing campaign targeting and customer lifetime value optimization in insurance portfolios.

# Model Characteristics

- **Algorithm:** lightgbm_classifier
- **Problem type:** binary_classification
- **Target column:** Response
- **Training samples:** 381,109
- **Features:** 10

# Data Overview

Trained on the Kaggle dataset [anmolkumar/health-insurance-cross-sell-prediction](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/anmolkumar/health-insurance-cross-sell-prediction). Encode categorical columns (Gender, Vehicle_Age, Vehicle_Damage, Region_Code, Policy_Sales_Channel) using target encoding or LightGBM's native categorical handling. Annual_Premium is right-skewed; apply log1p transform. No missing values present. Vintage represents days since policy inception; keep as-is.

**Feature columns used:** Gender, Age, Driving_License, Region_Code, Previously_Insured, Vehicle_Age, Vehicle_Damage, Annual_Premium, Policy_Sales_Channel, Vintage

# Evaluation Results

Evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation, compared against a naive baseline.

| | Model | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| ROC_AUC (mean) | 0.8575 | 0.5000 |
| ROC_AUC (std) | 0.0008 | 0.0000 |

Metric direction: higher is better.
